segments.title: Chương 186: 0186【Cạnh tranh ngành gay gắt】
segments.content:
Chapter 189: 0186 Fierce Industry Competition

Before Li Ao could even start beefing with people, Sina Blog had already made a move.

They probably saw how popular Kaixin001 became after "inviting" Li Ao, so they turned around and invited Li Ao's daughter, Li Wen.

Li Wen was currently residing in Beijing.

And she had already published four books in mainland China: one called *Cursing Along with Li Ao*, another called *Li Wen's Collection of Laughs*, and two English tutoring books.

Now, Li Wen was writing books, appearing on shows, giving English teaching lectures, and busying herself with lawsuits.

She was fighting six lawsuits at the same time, all of which she had initiated against others. In some cases, she only demanded 1 yuan in compensation from the other party.

She called herself a "female fighter" and even said she had written her will and was ready to become a "female martyr." Because she had received death threats, an assassin was already after her.

In less than three years of living in Beijing, she had already moved to five different residential communities. In her current community, she had been renting for only eight months but had already filed over 100 complaints with the property management office—something she boasted about to reporters.

In her book, she exposed her own upbringing, even writing about being sexually harassed by her stepfather and publishing his photo. She also said her current neighbors were all nouveau riche, detailing their various unseemly behaviors…

She insisted she wasn't doing these things for publicity, but to introduce China's friends to excellent Western moral values.

Her mother was abandoned by Li Ao back then, but she didn't resent her biological father. On the contrary, she praised Li Ao as a romantic and talented scholar who had ten or twenty girlfriends and was deeply and genuinely in love with every single woman.

This lady was just... something else!

Dorm room.

Chen Guiliang clicked open Li Wen's Sina Blog. This lady's very first blog post had an explosive number of views.

Li Wen's blog post was just a simple introduction to her home.

She was renting a villa in a certain part of Beijing and had a dedicated room for her clothes and shoes. Several hundred pieces of clothing, over two hundred pairs of shoes, all expensive brand names.

The set of photos showing off her house and luxury goods was posted, attracting a large crowd of netizens. Quite a few made sarcastic remarks, but even more fawned over her. Supporters and opponents even started flame wars in her blog's comment section.

Li Wen's second blog post was to show off her rockery. That is, in the villa she was renting, she had spent tens of thousands of yuan to build a rockery to decorate the lawn.

Chen Guiliang looked at the fawning remarks in the comments section and muttered, "I invite Li Ao to write online articles, and Sina invites his daughter to blog. What kind of monster have they unleashed ahead of time? Is Sina Blog going to turn into Xiaohongshu?"

"This woman, isn't she afraid of provoking the netizens' resentment of the rich?" Jiang Junlai was also sitting next to Chen Guiliang, checking out the blog.

Chen Guiliang laughed. "A woman who complains to property management over 200 times in 8 months, do you think she'd be afraid of netizens' insults? She's suing six people at the same time right now. She'll probably sue netizens next."

Not only did Li Wen constantly file lawsuits, but she would also write about the process of suing people into a rights-defense book titled *Li Wen Reasons*—and earn another round of royalties.

She was making money hand over fist.

The new roommate, Li Heng, said, "She's really embarrassing her father!"

Just then, Senior Min Wenyu, who had already moved to the floor above, came over with materials on several students from a mountainous region.

"When I went to volunteer-teach during the summer break, they were already implementing the 'Two Exemptions, One Subsidy' policy over there," Min Wenyu said. "Elementary school students are exempt from 260 yuan in tuition per person per year, and middle school students are exempt from 450 yuan per person per year."

Chen Guiliang said, "So they basically don't have to pay anything."

Min Wenyu said, "They still have to pay. There are book fees and miscellaneous fees. But for all of Caiyun Province, it's only been implemented for just over two million students this year. There are still more impoverished areas waiting for the policy to be implemented."

"Things have to be done gradually," Chen Guiliang said with understanding.

Min Wenyu said, "At the place where I volunteer-taught, the mountain children now only pay about 100 yuan a year for books and miscellaneous fees. The problem is they have many children; two or three is normal, some even have four or five. Over 100 yuan a year for one child, and it adds up to a heavy burden when you have several kids."

"There's nothing we can do to help with that," Chen Guiliang said.

Min Wenyu said, "These are all hardworking students from difficult backgrounds who get excellent grades. I've chosen five in total. Two of them are still in elementary school in the mountains, and the other three are in middle school at the township's central school. If you want to sponsor them, you can send the money directly to their class teachers. I've already contacted them."

Li Heng asked, "Why not send it to the students' parents?"

"The class teachers won't misuse the money, but the parents might," Min Wenyu said.

Chen Guiliang carefully looked through the materials on these poor students. Min Wenyu even gave suggested sponsorship amounts: for elementary school students, sponsor 80 yuan a year for books and miscellaneous fees, and 200 yuan for living expenses. For middle school students, sponsor 120 yuan a year for books and miscellaneous fees, 100 yuan for boarding fees, and 500 yuan for living expenses.

For these five poor students with excellent grades, Chen Guiliang only needed to sponsor 2720 yuan a year to help them complete their current stage of education.

"Alright, I'll send the money to their class teachers this weekend," Chen Guiliang said.

Jiang Junlai said, "You might as well launch a donation drive on 校内网 or Kaixin001. That way you could sponsor more students."

Chen Guiliang shook his head. "The websites I have won't proactively launch student aid projects, but they won't stop users from launching them. For user-initiated projects, the most the website will do is give some traffic. We will absolutely not get involved with the specific donations. That kind of thing is very troublesome. Sponsoring these five students will be a personal, anonymous donation. Don't go spreading it around."

"Don't worry, we won't blab."

"What's there not to talk about?"

"Exactly, donating to poor students is a good thing."

"I don't want the trouble. I just want to do my part."

Min Wenyu said, "This winter break, I plan to go to Qian Province to volunteer-teach. I'll pick a few more sponsorship candidates for you then."

Jiang Junlai said, "That's my hometown. I'll go with you!"

The next day, Chen Guiliang braced himself and went to his advanced mathematics class.

It was a required course starting this year, and Chen Guiliang felt it would be very difficult for him. However, it didn't affect most students from the Yuanpei Program, as they had already taken it during their freshman year.

It was almost noon when Chen Guiliang finally rushed to the company.

He passed by Senior Li Fan's desk, glanced at her computer, and said, "Scouting the enemy?"

Li Fan pointed at the screen. "Li Wen posted on her blog again. One post a day. If this keeps up, she might become more popular than Xu Jinglei."

"What's she showing off today?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Li Fan said, "She didn't show off her wealth today. Instead, she complained about her neighbor spitting on the ground, mocked the neighbor for being nouveau riche, and said that despite living in a villa, the neighbor has no refinement. Then she expanded on that to discuss the current quality of the nation's citizens. She said that China is developing too quickly now, but the overall quality of its citizens can't keep up. In less than half a day, this article has already gotten more than ten thousand views."

Chen Guiliang sighed with feeling. "This woman really knows how to grab eyeballs."

Sina Blog had dug up a real "treasure" this time!

"How's the data for the other blog sites?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Li Fan opened a spreadsheet file. "Most of the smaller blog sites have dismal data. BlogChina, which used to have the largest user base, has lost a large number of high-quality bloggers since Sina Blog went online. For the well-known bloggers who are still on BlogChina, I've been tracking their new posts' first-day and three-day cumulative views, and they've been on a downward trend. So far, the views have dropped by about 20% overall."
